definitions.explanation: A person's outward appearance, especially in terms of clothing and grooming. Often used when commenting on whether someone is well- or poorly-dressed.

examples.english: To pay attention to one's appearance.

examples.japanese: きちんとした{身|み}なりで{面接|めんせつ}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to the interview in neat attire.

examples.japanese: {身|み}なりがだらしないと、{第一印象|だいいちいんしょう}が{悪|わる}くなることがある。
examples.english: If your appearance is sloppy, it can make a bad first impression.

notes:
Focuses specifically on clothing and grooming rather than facial features or body shape. Often appears in contexts about social expectations and professionalism.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {身|み}なりに{気|き}をつける (pay attention to one's appearance)
- {身|み}なりを{整|ととの}える (tidy up one's appearance)
- きちんとした{身|み}なり (neat appearance)
- {身|み}なりがだらしない (sloppy appearance)
- みすぼらしい{身|み}なり (shabby appearance)
